CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010342242022 Case Number :EX/0000002/2023 KRISHNAMURTHY G versus SATHISH M Date : 01-08-2024 Business : Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR filed IA.No.II U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC, seeking for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose perform ministerial act of this court. Heard. The learned counel for DHR urged that, in this case this court granted relief of specific performance of contract by passing judgment and decree in O.S.No.4555/2020 dated 02.07.2022. As per the said judgment and decree the JDR is requires to execute sale deed in favour of DHR petitioner within 3 months from the date judgment. The JDR fails to execute sale deed by receiving remaining balance sale consideration. Hence, prays for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose of execution of sale deed on behalf of JDR. I have perused the IA.No.I, petition and decree. In O.S.No.4555/2020 this court decreed the suit of the plaintiff and directed to defendant execute the sale deed by receiving sale consideration within 3 months from 02.07.2022. There is no record to show that, the judgement passed by this court is setaside or stayed by competant court of law. It is just and proper to appointment of court commissioner for performing minsterial act on behalf of this court. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER IA.No.II filed U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC is hereby consider as filed U/o 26 rule 10-B of CPC and hereby allowed. One Advocate of Advocate’s Bar Bengaluru is appointed as court commissioner. The learned counsel for DHR filed memo with draft sale deed. Call on by 08.08.2024. Next Purpose : HEARING Next Hearing Date : 08-08-2024 CCH64 LXIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

--- NEXT ORDER ---

Thasildhar has been duly served, under which this court had sought the explanation to the salary drawing officer of the JDR herein for not attaching the salary of the JDR to satisfy the decree. The service of the show cause notice to the garnishee of the JDR has been reported to this court. Thus Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk has fails to send his explanation and fails to appear before this court, thus this court felt, it is proper to call the Spl. Thasildhar to be present before this court. Accordingly ordered to issue notice to the Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk Yelahanka, Bangalore to place his physicall appearance before this court on next date of hearing without fail. In this case, despite issuance of S/A/W to the garnishee of the JDR the same has not been carried out by the garnishee and despite service of show cause notice the garnishee remained absent. If that aspect is considered the garnishee may be hand in glow of the JDR, with intend to frustrate the decree of this court. Thus this court felt it is proper to order for issue arrest notice to the JDR. Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on IA.No. 2. As the DHR made out the grounds that it is the JDR and his garnishee with intend to frustrate the decree are evading the process of this court, thus IA.No. 2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed, ordered to issue arrest notice against the JDR, if the DHR pays the PF in the office. It is stated that Jdr No.1 is a proprietory concern represented by its proprietor Smt.Bhuvaneshwari, Said Smt.Bhuvaneshwari died on 05.02.2023. The present execution petition is filed to execute the joint memo filed in Crl.A No.1077/2021 before the lok adalath. The said Crl.A. No.1077/2021 was disposed in terms of joint memo on 25.06.2022. The Appellant having not complied with the terms of joint memo the present execution is filed. The said case in Crl.A. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010007192023 Case Number :EX/0000104/2023 LAKSHMAMMA versus SPL LAO KIADB Date : 04-08-2023 Business : Statement of objection have been filed by JDR advocate. As per statement of objection cheque bearing no. 230962 dated 29.03.2014 of Rs.1,84,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 215 of Bheemanakuppe Village has been numbered as LAC 57/2014 and the same day the JDR has sent another cheque bearing no.230963 dated 29.03.2014 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 205 of Bheemanakuppe Village, which was numbered as LAC 64/2014. It is stated that the office while registering the above cases with regard to amount in LAC 64/2014 have deposited the amount of Rs.1,84,00,000/- instead of Rs. 1,18,00,000/- and vice versa. The office while depositing the amount in LAC 57/2014 have deposited a sum of Rs.1,18,00,000/- instead of Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of both the records in LAC 57/2014 and 64/2014 it is seen that with regard to LAC 64/2014 the BDA has sent letter dated 09.04.2014 along with cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of record in LAC 57/2014 it is seen that BDA has sent letter No.885/09-10 cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/-. There is mistake committed by the office in taking the cheques in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014. Hence, the amount deposited in respect of cheque no.230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 57/2014 and the amount deposited in respect of cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 64/2014. Copy of this order to be entered in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014 . Call on 22-08-2023. Next Purpose : NOTICE Next Hearing Date : 22-08-2023 CCH17 II ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

Reissue A/W/M against the JDR. DHR files IA.No. 2 U/s 151 of CPC to extend the police protections to the bailiff of this court to execute the A/W/M issued against the JDR on the ground that the JDR has obstructed for the execution of the A/W/M and also sought the break opening of the lock of the premises of the JDR\''s to attach his movables. The A/W/M issued by this court returned unexecuted with a report that the JDR has obstructed for the execution of A/w/M and thus he sought the police protection. By considering the same this court is of the opinion as the JDR is obstructing for the execution of warrant it is proper to order the Jurisdictional Rajgopalanagar PS to extend the police security to the bailiff of this court to execute the A/W/M issued against the JDR. And also ordered to the bailiff to break open the lock of the premises of the JDR if his premises is kept locked to prevent the execution of warrant when he visits to the JDR\''s place for execution. Office is to send intimation to the Jurisdictional Rajgopalanagar PS to extend the police security to the bailiff of this court to execute the A/W/M issued against the JDR. Call on 01.06.2023 Next Purpose : NOTICE Next Hearing Date : 01-06-2023 CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

--- NEXT ORDER ---

CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010016892023 Case Number :EX/0000215/2023 BHAGYAMMA versus YELE GOWDA Date : 30-08-2023 Business : The Delivery warrant issued against the JDR returned unexecuted as kept locked and also reported that the JDR has inducted the tenants in the petition schedule property. As the decree for possession, the tenants under the possession of the JDR are bound by the decree. Thus this court felt they are not necessary party before this court to issue notice to them. Considering the same, this court felt proper to re-issue Delivery warrant with directions to break open the lock of the petition schedule property. The DHR files IA.No.2 u/O 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to break open the locks of the petition schedule properties and to deliver the vacant possession in favor of the DHR herein. As the JDR is obstructing the executing the Delivery warrant by kept locking the petition schedule property and appears to be inducted some 3rd party into the petition schedule property to delay the execution proceedings. Thus IA.No.2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Ordered to issue Delivery warrant with directions to the bailiff to break open the lock of the petition schedule property and demolish the building stands on the petition schedule property with the assistance of the men and material of the DHR and deliver the vacant petition schedule property in favour of the DHR. Directed the DHR to extend with sufficient men and material to demolish the building found on the petition schedule property. And also directed the jurisdictional Hebbal police to extend the police protection to the officer of this court to execute the Delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favor of the DHR herein. Call on 09.11.2023. Next Purpose : HEARING Next Hearing Date : 09-11-2023 CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

--- NEXT ORDER ---

CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010016892023 Case Number :EX/0000215/2023 BHAGYAMMA versus YELE GOWDA Date : 15-07-2023 Business : Sri LB files vakalath for JDR and files IA.No. 1 u/o 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to issue delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the existed structure with the police protections. In this case, the DHR has got the decree for possession wherein, directed the JDR herein to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the building existed therein within 90 days from the date of Judgment. The Judgment dt 27.01.2022 and the JDR submitted the against the Judgment and decree of this cour the JDR has not preferred an appeal, thus this court felt as the JDR is fails to comply the Judgment and Decree, thus it is proper to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favour of DHR herein by executing the delivery warrant. Accordingly IA.No. 1 is hereby allowed, delivery warrant is been issued to deliver the petition schedule property in favour of the DHR herein and permitted the bailiff of this court to take sufficient assistance to demolish the building existed on petition schedule property. Thus directed the DHR to extend his all assistance by providing men and machinery to carryout the demolition work and liberty is being given to the DHR to file calculation memo on the expenditure made for the demolition to recover from the JDR. To avoid the obstruction if any to come in the way of bailiff to execute the warrant to deliver the possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the structure therein it is proper to extend police security. Thus directed the police inspector attached to the Jurisdiction Hebbal Police station to extend the police protections to the officer of this court to execute the warrant as and when he approaches the police station by providing sufficient men. For await report. Call on 30.08.2023 Next Purpose : SUMMONS Next Hearing Date : 30-08-2023 CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

Accordingly IA.No. 1 is hereby allowed, delivery warrant is been issued to deliver the petition schedule property in favour of the DHR herein and permitted the bailiff of this court to take sufficient assistance to demolish the building existed on petition schedule property. Thus directed the DHR to extend his all assistance by providing men and machinery to carryout the demolition work and liberty is being given to the DHR to file calculation memo on the expenditure made for the demolition to recover from the JDR. To avoid the obstruction if any to come in the way of bailiff to execute the warrant to deliver the possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the structure therein it is proper to extend police security. Thus directed the police inspector attached to the Jurisdiction Hebbal Police station to extend the police protections to the officer of this court to execute the warrant as and when he approaches the police station by providing sufficient men. Decree Holder present. Learned counsel for Decree Holder present. Judgment Debtor absent. She filed I.A.No.4 under Order XXI Rule 43 of CPC for attachment of movable property as per the inventory made by the bailiff and I.A.No.5 under Order XXI Rule 64 of CPC for sale of movable properties by public action. Heard the counsel for DHR on I.A.No.4 and 5. Perused the record. The DHR has filed EP for execution of decree in OS.No.2524/2022 for delivery warrant and also for recovery of arrears of rent. As per the report of bailiff dated 07/03/2023, the possession of the schedule premises has been delivered to the DHR. In view of reasons, I.A.No.4 and 5 are allowed, the movable properties of the JDR as per the inventory of the bailiff are attached and ordered to be sold in public action. Issue sale proclamation of movables of the JDR, the spot sale is fixed by giving 07 days time from the date on which the copy of the proclamation has been affixed on the Court house, as required under Order XXI Rule 68 of CPC. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010019752023 Case Number :EX/0000231/2023 SAVITHRAMMA versus MUNISIDAPPA K SINCE DEAD BY HIS LRS JAYAMMA Date : 22-09-2023 Business : Delivery warrant is duly executed. Perused the bailiff report and spot mahazar. On perusal of it, it appears that the vacant possession of petition schedule premises has been handed over to the Dhr. In view of this, I feel it is just and proper to close the petition as E.F.S. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDERS The petition is ordered to be closed as E.F.S. Nature of Disposal : DISPOSED OTHERWISE Disposal Date : 22-09-2023 CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

--- NEXT ORDER ---

Back Daily Status PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE In the court of :CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010019752023 Case Number :EX/0000231/2023 SAVITHRAMMA versus MUNISIDAPPA K SINCE DEAD BY HIS LRS JAYAMMA Date : 08-08-2023 Business : Heard the counsel for Dhr. In the instant case, Jdr.No.1 and 4 are placed exparte. Though sufficient time has been given Jdr.No.2 has not filed objection. Perused the judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has set-aside the judgment and decree passed by this court in O.S.2871/2003 and decreed the suit in favor of the plaintiffs. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has further held that judgment and decree passed in O.S.10476/1988 and in R.F.A.No.44/1996 are not binding on the plaintiffs and consequently declared the plaintiffs as the absolute owners of the suit schedule property and directed the legal representative of defendants to hand the vacant possession of the petitioin schedule property. In view of judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A. No.219/2014, I feel it is necessary to issue delivery warrant against the legal representatives of defendant/Jdrs herein. Further, as per office note, no stay or appeal pending against judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. Hence, issue delivery warrant against Jdrs to hand over the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the Dhr. R/by 22.09.2023. In the instant case, Jdr.No.1 and 4 are placed exparte. Though sufficient time has been given Jdr.No.2 has not filed objection. Perused the judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has set-aside the judgment and decree passed by this court in O.S.2871/2003 and decreed the suit in favor of the plaintiffs. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has further held that judgment and decree passed in O.S.10476/1988 and in R.F.A.No.44/1996 are not binding on the plaintiffs and consequently declared the plaintiffs as the absolute owners of the suit schedule property and directed the legal representative of defendants to hand the vacant possession of the petitioin schedule property. In view of judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A. No.219/2014, I feel it is necessary to issue delivery warrant against the legal representatives of defendant/Jdrs herein. Further, as per office note, no stay or appeal pending against judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. Hence, issue delivery warrant against Jdrs to hand over the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the Dhr. R/by 22.09.2023. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010020582023 Case Number :EX/0000233/2023 BOPAIAH K K versus SANGANA GOUDA B PATIL Date : 26-07-2024 Business : DHR has filed this execution petition against the JDR for decreetal amount of Rs.44150 including interest from 15.01.2022 till 15.01.2023 at the rate of 12 percent p.a of Rs57395 The learned counsel for the JDR submitted that, as per the decree he has paid the entire amount and he is not liable to pay any interest. On going through the materials placed before me, this petition is filed against the judgment passed by the trial court in C.C.No.6126-2014 and judgment passed by this Court in Crl.A.No.542-2015 and order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka in Crl.R.P.No.889-2016 C/W 770-2016 before lok adalath. On going through the said order of the Hon\\\''ble High Court of Karnataka the respondent Sangana Gouda B Patil i.e the JDR herein undertook to pay the sum of Rs.8,25,000 to the present DHR and in turn the present DHR is permitted to withdraw an amount of Rs.3,83,50- deposited before the Trial Court and balance amount of Rs.4,41,500 is to be paid by the present JDR to the present DHR within 6 months from the date of the said order. On going through the order sheet the JDR has filed D.D. for Rs.2,00,000 on 21.12.2023 and again on 25.01.2024 he has handed over 2 D.Ds for an amount of Rs.1,00,000 and Rs.41,500 to the counsel for the DHR. Again on 13.03.2024 JDR filed D.D for Rs.1,00,00-. In total JDR has paid 4,41,500. Hence, it is clear that the JDR has already paid Rs.4,41,500 as ordered by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and this petition is filed for collecting interest at the rate of 12percent p.a, which nowhere finds place in the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and it has not discussed regarding the interest.In the circumstances, without any speaking order DHR is not entitled to receive 12 percent interest on the principal amount. As on now, the JDR has paid the entire decreetal amount as per the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka. Hence, to report closure of execution petition by 08.08.2024. Next Purpose : HEARING Next Hearing Date : 08-08-2024 CCH69 LXVIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010020582023 Case Number :EX/0000233/2023 BOPAIAH K K versus SANGANA GOUDA B PATIL Date : 26-07-2024 Business : DHR has filed this execution petition against the JDR for decreetal amount of Rs.44150 including interest from 15.01.2022 till 15.01.2023 at the rate of 12 percent p.a of Rs57395 The learned counsel for the JDR submitted that, as per the decree he has paid the entire amount and he is not liable to pay any interest. On going through the materials placed before me, this petition is filed against the judgment passed by the trial court in C.C.No.6126-2014 and judgment passed by this Court in Crl.A.No.542-2015 and order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka in Crl.R.P.No.889-2016 C/W 770-2016 before lok adalath. On going through the said order of the Hon\\\''ble High Court of Karnataka the respondent Sangana Gouda B Patil i.e the JDR herein undertook to pay the sum of Rs.8,25,000 to the present DHR and in turn the present DHR is permitted to withdraw an amount of Rs.3,83,50- deposited before the Trial Court and balance amount of Rs.4,41,500 is to be paid by the present JDR to the present DHR within 6 months from the date of the said order. On going through the order sheet the JDR has filed D.D. for Rs.2,00,000 on 21.12.2023 and again on 25.01.2024 he has handed over 2 D.Ds for an amount of Rs.1,00,000 and Rs.41,500 to the counsel for the DHR. Again on 13.03.2024 JDR filed D.D for Rs.1,00,00-. In total JDR has paid 4,41,500. Hence, it is clear that the JDR has already paid Rs.4,41,500 as ordered by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and this petition is filed for collecting interest at the rate of 12percent p.a, which nowhere finds place in the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and it has not discussed regarding the interest.In the circumstances, without any speaking order DHR is not entitled to receive 12 percent interest on the principal amount. As on now, the JDR has paid the entire decreetal amount as per the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka. Hence, to report closure of execution petition by 08.08.2024. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010017612023 Case Number :EX/0000259/2023 VITTAL KUMAR C versus MANIKYAMMA Date : 04-01-2025 Business : Perused the records. This execution petition is filed to execute the order passed in Misc 451/2013. As per records RFA No.1653/2021 is filed challenging the order dated:11.01.2021 passed in Misc 451/2013 which is sought to be executed. Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has directed to maintain the status – quo in all respect. Till the disposal of RFA No. 1653/2021 this court cannot proceed with this execution petition in view of order passed by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka on 13.12.2023 in RFA No. 1653/2021. Therefore the execution petition can be closed for the time being granting liberty to Decree-Holder to file fresh petition after disposal of RFA No. 1653/2021. Accordingly I pass following: ORDER The execution petition is closed for the time being in view of status – quo order passed by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No. 1653/2021. Liberty is granted to Decree-Holder to file fresh petition after disposal of RFA. Nature of Disposal : DISPOSED OTHERWISE Disposal Date : 04-01-2025 CCH44 XLIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE

CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010017612023 Case Number :EX/0000259/2023 VITTAL KUMAR C versus MANIKYAMMA Date : 04-01-2025 Business : Perused the records. This execution petition is filed to execute the order passed in Misc 451/2013. As per records RFA No.1653/2021 is filed challenging the order dated:11.01.2021 passed in Misc 451/2013 which is sought to be executed. Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has directed to maintain the status – quo in all respect. Till the disposal of RFA No. 1653/2021 this court cannot proceed with this execution petition in view of order passed by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka on 13.12.2023 in RFA No. 1653/2021. Therefore the execution petition can be closed for the time being granting liberty to Decree-Holder to file fresh petition after disposal of RFA No. 1653/2021. Accordingly I pass following: ORDER The execution petition is closed for the time being in view of status – quo order passed by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No. 1653/2021. Liberty is granted to Decree-Holder to file fresh petition after disposal of RFA. Nature of Disposal : DISPOSED OTHERWISE Disposal Date : 04-01-2025 CCH44 XLIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE

Back Daily Status PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE In the court of :CCH26 X ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010022972023 Case Number :EX/0000260/2023 LOKESH D versus PREMA K SINCE DEAD BY LRs PRABHAKAR S R Date : 13-02-2023 Business : Case advanced. The counsel for Dhr files memo seeking leave to withdraw the petition in view of the full satisfaction of the petition claim. However Sri GS advocate files power for Jdr along with I.A.No.2 U/sec 151 of CPC seeking to recall the order dtd.08.02.2023. He seeks for time to file objection in view of pendency of RFA before the Hon\''ble High Court. However no stay is granted. In view of the report of the bailiff dtd.10.02.2023 with regard to the due execution of delivery warrant and handing over possession of petition premises to the Dhr in presence of witnesses under the mahazar, the prayer of the counsel for Jdr is cannot be accepted since already the warrant is duly executed and the Jdr is shown to be out of possession of the schedule premises. Hence, the memo filed by the Dhr is hereby accepted and the EP is hereby closed as the claim of the petition is fully satisfied. Nature of Disposal : DISPOSED OTHERWISE Disposal Date : 13-02-2023 CCH26 X ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

--- NEXT ORDER ---

Issue similar direction to the concerned jurisdictional police to provide assistance to the court bailiff in execution of warrant. R/by 04.03.2023. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010024762023 Case Number :EX/0000267/2023 THIMMAIAHA SINCE DEAD BY HIS LR LALITHA T versus RAMESH Date : 17-03-2023 Business : This is a petition filed by the DHR to give direction to the jurisdictional police to give sufficient protection to the DHR The office raised objection regarding limitation. From the judgment or decree discloses that, the DHR got the partition and also the court held that the Plaintiff is entitled for permanent injunction and also restrained the defendant from dispossessing the Plaintiff from the Suit Schedule property. The Learned advocate for the DHR has argued that to enforce the DHR in permanent injunction suit limitation will not applicable. Hence, he requested to over rule the office objections. To substantiate his argument he is relied upon the judgment of the Hon\''ble Orissa High Court passed in Chakaradara patil (dead by LRS) Vs Geetha Bhava. I have gone through the judgment of the Orissa Hon\''ble High Court where in the Hon\''ble High Court held that as per the provision to article 136 of limitation act there is no limitation for execution of a decree for permanent injunction. Therefore the execution case in question cannot be said to be barred by law of limitation. This ruling is applicable to the case of the DHR since this court granted the injunction against the defendant and the DHR can enforce the decree when JDR violated the court order. Accordingly, office objection regarding the limitation is overruled. Issue notice to JDR, if PF is paid. Call on 20.06.2023. Next Purpose : NOTICE Next Hearing Date : 20-06-2023 CCH2 I ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

--- NEXT ORDER ---

This IA is filed by the DHR under Order VI Rule 17 of the CPC r/w Sec.151 of the CPC to delete existing suit schedule property and insert the property bearing No.484 as per decree. It is stated by the DHR that due to clerical error the schedule property is wrongly mentioned. JDR filed objection stating that the present schedule property mentioned in the EP is not related OS.6668/2014 and application is filed at belated stage. As per the decree passed in OS.6668/2014 the suit property is site No.484 situated at Mallathhalli Village but in Execution Petition the suit property is shown as the land bearing Sy.No.33 new Sy.No.93 of Mallasandra Village. So, it appears that due to clerical error the said mistake is occured in the petition. Hence, it can be corrected. This EP is filed to execute the decree in OS.6668/2014. Hence, the suit property is said suit has to be mentioned as suit property in this EP. Hence, IA.No.1 is allowed. DHR is permitted to amend the schedule of the EP. For amendment and amended petition. This IA is filed by the DHR under Order VI Rule 17 of the CPC r/w Sec.151 of the CPC to delete existing suit schedule property and insert the property bearing No.484 as per decree. It is stated by the DHR that due to clerical error the schedule property is wrongly mentioned. JDR filed objection stating that the present schedule property mentioned in the EP is not related OS.6668/2014 and application is filed at belated stage. As per the decree passed in OS.6668/2014 the suit property is site No.484 situated at Mallathhalli Village but in Execution Petition the suit property is shown as the land bearing Sy.No.33 new Sy.No.93 of Mallasandra Village. So, it appears that due to clerical error the said mistake is occured in the petition. Hence, it can be corrected. This EP is filed to execute the decree in OS.6668/2014. Hence, the suit property is said suit has to be mentioned as suit property in this EP. Hence, IA.No.1 is allowed. DHR is permitted to amend the schedule of the EP. For amendment and amended petition. Call on 17-10-2025. Next Purpose : SUMMONS Next Hearing Date : 17-10-2025 CCH43 XLII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE

CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010030302023 Case Number :EX/0000320/2023 MAHADEVA K C versus DODDAVEERAIAH Date : 09-02-2023 Business : Case is advanced. Along with the advance application, Mr. VR Advocate filed Vakalath for JDr. Both DHr and JDr and their Advocates are present. As there is a chance of settlement, matter is referred to Lok Adalath. PROCEEDINGS BEFORE LOK ADALATH (BENCH NO.3/2022) Both DHr and JDr and their Advocates are present. By virtue of the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.2117/2008, this execution petition was filed for recovery of Rs.6,40,244/-. After much persuasion by the Learned Counsel for DHr and JDr, both parties agreed for an amicable settlement and thereby DHr has agreed to receive the sum of Rs.3,80,000/- in full and final satisfaction of his claim. Accordingly, JDr has issued DD for Rs.3,80,000/- drawn on Union Bank of India, RMV Extension Branch, Bengaluru. As per consensus arrived between the parties, both parties filed a joint memo and after receiving the sum of Rs.3,80,000/-, both parties pray before the Lok Adalath to close the E.P. as fully satisfied. Since, the compromise arrived between the parties is in accordance with law, joint memo filed by them is accepted and thereby E.P. is closed as FS. Nature of Disposal : SETTLED IN LOK ADALATH Disposal Date : 09-02-2023 CCH8 XI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010007822023 Case Number :EX/0000117/2023 KARNATAKA BANK LIMITED versus RAVI KUMAR S Date : 22-08-2026 Business : Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. Upon perusal of order sheet, it is noticed that, on the earlier dates of hearing, the counsel for DHR was directed to take steps against JDR No.1 and 2 for the issuance of cause notices. Despite providing multiple opportunities, the DHR has failed to take proper steps against Jdr No.1 for taking steps to issue cause notices in order to effectively execute the decree. In view of the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025 and in compliance of the circular No.2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating the disposal of execution petitions within 6 months, this Court is duty bound to prevent undue pendency of the execution petitions. Since the DHR has not diligently pursued the execution and no purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending further, the execution petition deserves to be disposed of. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification. Nature of Disposal : DISPOSED OTHERWISE Disposal Date : 22-08-2026 CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010007822023 Case Number :EX/0000117/2023 KARNATAKA BANK LIMITED versus RAVI KUMAR S Date : 22-08-2026 Business : Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. Upon perusal of order sheet, it is noticed that, on the earlier dates of hearing, the counsel for DHR was directed to take steps against JDR No.1 and 2 for the issuance of cause notices. Despite providing multiple opportunities, the DHR has failed to take proper steps against Jdr No.1 for taking steps to issue cause notices in order to effectively execute the decree. In view of the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025 and in compliance of the circular No.2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating the disposal of execution petitions within 6 months, this Court is duty bound to prevent undue pendency of the execution petitions. Since the DHR has not diligently pursued the execution and no purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending further, the execution petition deserves to be disposed of. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification. Nature of Disposal : DISPOSED OTHERWISE Disposal Date : 22-08-2026 CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010045902023 Case Number :EX/0000447/2023 MARGADARSI CHITS KAR PVT LTD versus MAHESH T C Date : 29-03-2025 Business : The Decree holder and the learned counsel for the Decree holder are absent. ORDERS The decree holder filed this Execution Petition to execute the Recovery Certificate issued by the Deputy Registrar of Chits, 2nd Zone, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru in Dispute No.DRB-2/CFS/118/2019-20 under Section 71(a) of Chit Funds Act. The office has raised the objection stating that the judgment debtors are not residing within the jurisdiction of this Court. Heard the learned Counsel for the decree holder on the office objection. The learned Counsel for the decree holder relied the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case between Muneer Ahmed Sheriff and others V/s Javeeria Nusrath (ILR 2004 KAR 5254). In the light of the above, I perused the materials available on record. As stated above, this Execution Petition is filed by the decree holder against the judgment debtors to execute the Recovery Certificate issued by the Deputy Registrar of Chits, 2nd Zone, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru in Dispute No.DRB-2/CFS/118/2019-20 under Section 71(a) of Chit Funds Act. Among the judgment debtors, judgment debtor No.1 is residing at Nagamangala Taluk, judgments No.2, 4 and 6 are residing at Manya Taluk, judgment debtor No.3 is residing at Maddur Taluk and judgment debtor No.5 is residing at Pandavapura Taluk. The properties sought to be attached are situated not within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court. They are situated within the territorial jurisdictions of different Courts of Mandya District, Under Section 39(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Court has jurisdiction to execute the decree under execution against the judgment debtors and the property which is situated out side the local limits of this Court. Therefore, the office objection raised in this case is over ruled. To hear on I.A.No.1. Call on 21.06.2025. Next Purpose : HEARING Next Hearing Date : 21-06-2025 CCH14 XXXI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE CNR Number :KABC010045902023 Case Number :EX/0000447/2023 MARGADARSI CHITS KAR PVT LTD versus MAHESH T C Date : 29-03-2025 Business : The Decree holder and the learned counsel for the Decree holder are absent. ORDERS The decree holder filed this Execution Petition to execute the Recovery Certificate issued by the Deputy Registrar of Chits, 2nd Zone, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru in Dispute No.DRB-2/CFS/118/2019-20 under Section 71(a) of Chit Funds Act. The office has raised the objection stating that the judgment debtors are not residing within the jurisdiction of this Court. Heard the learned Counsel for the decree holder on the office objection. The learned Counsel for the decree holder relied the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case between Muneer Ahmed Sheriff and others V/s Javeeria Nusrath (ILR 2004 KAR 5254). In the light of the above, I perused the materials available on record. As stated above, this Execution Petition is filed by the decree holder against the judgment debtors to execute the Recovery Certificate issued by the Deputy Registrar of Chits, 2nd Zone, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru in Dispute No.DRB-2/CFS/118/2019-20 under Section 71(a) of Chit Funds Act. Among the judgment debtors, judgment debtor No.1 is residing at Nagamangala Taluk, judgments No.2, 4 and 6 are residing at Manya Taluk, judgment debtor No.3 is residing at Maddur Taluk and judgment debtor No.5 is residing at Pandavapura Taluk. The properties sought to be attached are situated not within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court. They are situated within the territorial jurisdictions of different Courts of Mandya District, Under Section 39(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Court has jurisdiction to execute the decree under execution against the judgment debtors and the property which is situated out side the local limits of this Court. Therefore, the office objection raised in this case is over ruled. To hear on I.A.No.1. Call on 21.06.2025. Next Purpose : HEARING Next Hearing Date : 21-06-2025 CCH14 XXXI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

Learned advocate for DHR filed a memo along with Certified copy of the memorandum of compromise petition filed U/o 23 Rule 3 of CPC in RFA no. 310/2023 and order passed in RFA no. 310/2023 dt. 08.06.2023. As per the condition no.9 of the aforesaid compromise petition and observation made in para no.9 at page no.6 of the order shows that, the plaintiff is entitled for the refund of additional court fee of Rs. 77,904/-. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka accepted the compromise entered between the parties, hence the plaintiff / DHR is entitled for the refund of said amount of Rs. 77,904/-. Hence the following; ORDER Accordingly, office is directed to refund additional court fee of Rs. 77,904/- to the plaintiff / DHR through E-payment in accordance with law.
